solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Yahoo endlessly crashing, start of conversation on board? (4)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: without its end, the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.crashing: letters that crash end up jumbled

blocks.note: the web name without its final O
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A web service keeps going down while someone opens a conversation aboard.
annotation.walkthrough: Yahoo here is the old search engine, which makes 'crashing' read as a computer failure rather than an instruction to jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: A sailor's hail used to open talk with another vessel or someone aboard, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: A river flowed in Scottish isle (5)

blocks.note: taken as it stands
R is the map abbreviation for river
water that flowed ran

annotation.surface: A river once ran across a Scottish island.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole answer is built from plain pieces; the only knowledge needed is the island's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an island in the Firth of Clyde, off Scotland's west coast.

entries.clue: Have now to get head down (3)

indicatorNotes.to get head down: in a down entry the head is the top letter; moving it down sends it to the bottom

blocks.note: taken as it stands
the N at the head moves to the foot

annotation.surface: An instruction to put your head down and get on with it right now.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head down' sounds like knuckling down to work; in a down clue it tells you to move the first letter to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to possess.

entries.clue: Recent arrival, fantastic wee bairn regularly visited (6)

indicatorNotes.fantastic: something fantastic is fanciful, so the letters are reshaped
indicatorNotes.regularly visited: letters visited at regular intervals, here the first, third and fifth

blocks.note: taken as it stands, to be jumbled
the odd letters of B-A-I-R-N
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A newborn Scottish baby has had lots of visitors.
annotation.walkthrough: Bairn is Scots for child and wee means small, so the surface is a new baby being visited, which is just what the answer describes.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal word for a newcomer, someone who has only just arrived in a group.

entries.clue: Discharge former partner due for relocation (5)

indicatorNotes.for relocation: letters relocated are moved into a new order

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
DUE rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone is about to throw out their ex, who is due to be moved on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' reads like dismissing the ex; it is the verb for oozing out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to ooze or give off slowly, as a plant does sap.

entries.clue: Seeing bear? (9)

blocks.note: the literary verb for looking at something
to bear a weight is to be carrying it, read as two words

annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BE HOLDING and it means to bear, as you bear a load; the question mark flags that the second sense is a pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Seeing and this word share the sense of looking at something; the literary verb is behold.

entries.clue: Put up article in Spanish on Peron, perhaps with note (7)

indicatorNotes.with: one piece goes with, alongside, the next

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
Eva Perón, Argentina's first lady; 'perhaps' says she is one Peron of several
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: Someone posts a Spanish-language article about Peron, with a footnote.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like publishing the article; it is the definition. Peron is Juan too, which is why 'perhaps' is needed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to raise something is to put it up.

entries.clue: Younger relative, dad-hugger, ran amok? Give it time (13)

indicatorNotes.amok: letters running amok go wild, out of order
indicatorNotes.Give it: add the next piece to the mix

blocks.note: twelve letters to be jumbled
T is the abbreviation for time
anagram indicator: all thirteen letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A child who clings to her father runs wild; give her time and she will settle.
annotation.walkthrough: The T has to be added to the fodder before jumbling: 'Give it time' tells you to throw it in.
annotation.definitionFit: A child's daughter is two generations younger than you, so a younger relative.

entries.clue: Doctor having drink and kebab (5)

indicatorNotes.having: the outer piece has the inner one inside it

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
as in 'I'll have one', a drink

annotation.surface: A doctor is out for drinks and a kebab.
annotation.walkthrough: D(ONE)R. The answer is the standard late-night British takeaway kebab.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the layered spit-roasted meat is one kind of kebab.

entries.clue: Settle dodgy scene involving politician (8)

indicatorNotes.dodgy: something dodgy is not straight, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.involving: the jumbled letters involve, take in, the politician

blocks.note: SCENE rearranged
CON is short for Conservative, a UK party member

annotation.surface: Someone tries to smooth over a shady incident involving an MP.
annotation.walkthrough: ENS(CON)CE. 'Settle' pretends to mean settle a dispute; it means to settle comfortably into a place.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to settle yourself snugly into a place.

entries.clue: Cry as water’s broken inside baby’s membrane (9)

indicatorNotes.broken: the word is broken up and reassembled
indicatorNotes.inside: the jumbled letters go inside the membrane

blocks.note: a caul is the membrane sometimes covering a newborn's head
WATER rearranged

annotation.surface: A mother cries out as her waters break during labour.
annotation.walkthrough: C(ATERW)AUL. The 's in water's is 'is', so 'water is broken' supplies the jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: A cat's wailing howl, so a loud unpleasant cry.

entries.clue: Lot of love cherished by boy (4)

indicatorNotes.cherished by: held close, and so inside, the boy

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
love is nil in tennis, and nil is O

annotation.surface: A boy treasures a great deal of love.
annotation.walkthrough: L(O)AD. 'Lot of love' reads as one phrase; 'Lot' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Informally, this word for a burden means a great amount, a lot.

entries.clue: Surprisingly alert from birth and unconventional (11)

indicatorNotes.Surprisingly: letters arranged surprisingly end up in an unexpected order

blocks.note: ALERT rearranged
a native speaker has spoken the language from birth

annotation.surface: A baby who was remarkably alert from the moment of birth, and rather unusual.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From birth' is not a letter instruction but a definition of its own: what you are from birth is native.
annotation.definitionFit: Used of lifestyles, music or medicine outside the mainstream, so unconventional.

entries.clue: Unprofessional team at Euros bottles it (7)

indicatorNotes.bottles it: the phrase holds the answer bottled up inside it

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'team' through 'at' into the start of 'Euros'

annotation.surface: An unprofessional football team chokes at the European Championship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottles it' is British slang for losing your nerve, which is what the surface uses it for; the Euros is football's European Championship.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone not paid for the work, whence the sense of unskilled or unprofessional.

entries.clue: One to win over (5)

blocks.note: a, as in one of something
to gain is to win

annotation.surface: One person trying to win another over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Win over' looks like one phrase meaning persuade; 'over' stands alone as the definition, as in 'do it over'.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Do it over' means do it once more.

entries.clue: Just beautiful (4)

blocks.note: just as an adjective: impartial, even-handed
the old poetic sense of lovely

annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' pretends to be the adverb meaning only; it is the adjective meaning impartial.
annotation.definitionFit: Double definition: the everyday sense of impartial, and the old poetic sense of lovely.

entries.clue: Boss kit for bowler? (8)

blocks.note: the head is the boss
kit and gear are both equipment

annotation.surface: A club captain handing out cricket kit for the bowler.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, where a bowler delivers the ball; here it is the bowler hat, and the question mark says it is one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a bowler is a hard round felt hat.

entries.clue: Having a shock may be frightening (5)

blocks.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair
informal for scary, as a risky moment is

annotation.surface: Receiving a sudden shock can be frightening.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as a fright; it is a shock of hair.
annotation.definitionFit: Double definition: covered in hair, as a head with a shock of it is, and the slang sense of scary.

entries.clue: Liberal member getting stuck into beer (5)

indicatorNotes.getting stuck into: the member goes into the beer

blocks.note: ale is a beer
Member of Parliament

annotation.surface: A Liberal Democrat MP knocking back the beer.
annotation.walkthrough: A(MP)LE. The capital L makes 'Liberal' look like the party; it is the adjective meaning generous.
annotation.definitionFit: Liberal means generous in amount, as a liberal helping is a big one.

entries.clue: Familial ties developing, sister on lap accepts greeting (13)

indicatorNotes.developing: the letters develop into a new form
indicatorNotes.accepts: the jumbled letters accept the greeting inside them

blocks.note: SISTER ON LAP rearranged, to be split before the last two letters
hi is a greeting

annotation.surface: Family bonds grow as a little sister sits on someone's lap and says hello.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sister on lap' paints a cosy family picture, so the fodder barely looks like fodder; the jumble must leave a gap for the greeting near its end.
annotation.definitionFit: Ties between people, of which family ones are familial.

entries.clue: Builder’s assistant wearing boots, say, with no top (3)

indicatorNotes.with no top: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which goes

blocks.note: shod means wearing shoes, boots being one kind
the S at the top goes

annotation.surface: A builder's mate in work boots but no shirt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With no top' plays on being shirtless; it removes the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The open trough on a pole used by a labourer to carry bricks up to the builder.

entries.clue: Broadcasts about poems (6)

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
a lay is a narrative poem or song

annotation.surface: A radio station airs programmes about poetry.
annotation.walkthrough: A lay is an old word for a narrative poem, as in Macaulay's Lays of Ancient Rome.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to pass on a signal or programme is to broadcast it.

entries.clue: Margin of advantage (4)

blocks.note: the border or rim of something
a slight lead over a rival

annotation.walkthrough: 'Margin of advantage' reads as one phrase, a winning margin; split it into two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Double definition: the border of something, and the lead that decides a contest.
